//: Provider catalogue. Read by both Omagif.qml (via a FileView) and by ./setup, so a provider's human-facing details are stated exactly once. The matching request/parse logic lives in providers/<Id>.js — see providers/README.md.
//mediaHosts: Hosts a provider's image URLs are allowed to live on, matched as the host itself or any subdomain of it. Media URLs are read out of a remote response, so nothing downloads or displays until its host is on this list and its scheme is https. bin/omagif-action enforces the union of every entry's list — see the header there.

providers.label: Giphy
providers.keyHint: Create an app, choose the API (not the SDK), and copy its API key.

providers.label: Giphy (no API key)
providers.caveat: Reads Giphy's public search page instead of its API, so there is nothing to sign up for. In exchange: about 25 results per search with no scrolling for more, no rating or language filter, and it stops working if Giphy redesigns that page. Add a Giphy API key for the full picker.
providers.keyHint: Nothing to do — this provider needs no key.

providers.label: Tenor
providers.disabledReason: Google stopped accepting new Tenor API clients in January 2026. The v2 endpoint still serves existing keys, so this stays selectable for anyone who already has one — set enabled to true if they reopen signups.
providers.keyHint: Create a Google Cloud project, enable the Tenor API, then make an API key.

providers.label: Tenor (no API key)
providers.caveat: Reads Tenor's public search page instead of its API — the only way a new install can use Tenor at all, since Google stopped issuing API keys in January 2026. Heavy on traffic: Tenor serves much larger GIFs than Giphy, so one search pulls roughly 15-20 MB of previews and a single GIF you copy can be 10-20 MB. Think twice on a metered or slow connection. Also: about 49 results per search with no scrolling for more, no content filter, and it stops working if Tenor redesigns that page.
providers.keyHint: Nothing to do — this provider needs no key.
